chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazem, who said: 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn al-Qasim al-Ansari narrated to me, saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated to us

that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and said: 'I am ruined, I am ruined!' So he said: 'And what has ruined you?' He said: 'I approached my wife during the month of Ramadan while I was fasting.' The Prophet said to him: 'Free a slave.' He said: 'I cannot find [one].' He said: 'Then fast for two consecutive months.' He said: 'I cannot handle it.' He said: 'Give charity to sixty poor people.' He said: 'I cannot find [the means].' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) was brought a 'irq or a 'muktal containing fifteen sa's of dates. The Prophet said to him: 'Take it and give it as charity.' He said: 'By He who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, between its two 'laba's, there is no household more in need of it than us.' So he said: 'Take it and eat it, you and your family, for indeed, it is an expiation for you.'

key_terms.سِتُّونَ مِسْكِينًا: Sixty poor people, the number of recipients for the charity expiation
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: Two consecutive months, a specific condition for the fasting expiation
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods
key_terms.عِرْق: A specific measure or container for dates, often referring to a bundle or sack
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or atonement for a religious violation
key_terms.مُكْتَل: A large basket or container used for holding dates or grain

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of expiation for breaking the fast in Ramadan due to sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* elucidates the specific expiation (kaffarah) for breaking the Ramadan fast through sexual intercourse, establishing a hierarchical progression of obligations based on financial and physical capacity. It highlights the Prophet’s practical wisdom in providing the man with dates, which the man initially deemed too valuable for personal consumption, yet the Prophet clarified they served as the expiation itself, illustrating the flexibility in applying religious duties to individual circumstances.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Musa bin Hasan, from Muhammed bin Abdul-Hameed, from Saif bin ‘Umayra, from Mansur bin Hazem, that he said: I was told by Abdul-Mo’min ibn Qasem al-Ansari, that he said: We were told by Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him,

that a man came to the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and he said: I am to perish! I am to perish! So he said: And what will cause you to perish? He said: I (sexually) approached my woman during the Month of Ramadhan whilst I was fasting. The Prophet then said to him: Liberate a neck (in captivity). He said: I cannot find. He said: Then fast for two consecutive months. He said: I cannot handle. He said: Give charity to sixty needy ones. He said: I cannot find (affordability). He said: Then the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, was given ‘irq or mukattal in which there were fifteen saa’ [1] of dates. The Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, then said: Take it and give it as charity. He said: By He who sent you with the truth as a Prophet, between its two laba’s, there is no household more in need of it than us. So he said: Take it and eat it, you and your family, for indeed, it is an expiation to you.
